title.value: Predicting the probability distribution of bus travel time to measure the reliability of public transport services
title.justification: This is the title of the paper.
title.quote:
Predicting the probability distribution of bus travel time to measure
the reliability of public transport services

extractions.description: This paper compares probabilistic models for predicting the conditional probability density function (PDF) of bus travel time and proposes a simulation framework to approximate the expected secondary delays, a measure of the reliability of public transport services. It uses a dataset of more than 41,000 trips and 50 bus routes of the city of Montréal to compare similarity-based density estimation models and a smoothed logistic regression model.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on improving the reliability of public transport services using probabilistic models. While this can contribute to making public transport more attractive, it doesn't directly address broader sustainability issues.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote:
An important aspect of the quality of a public transport service is its reliability, which is defined
as the invariability of the service attributes. In order to measure reliability during the service
planning phase, a key piece of information is the long-term prediction of the density of the
travel time, which conveys the uncertainty of travel times

primary_category.justification: Improving public transport reliability encourages ridership and reduces reliance on private vehicles, contributing to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions from transportation.
primary_category.quote:
In order to increase ridership and attract new users, public transport agencies put increasing emphasis on improving the quality
of the service they provide and particularly its regularity, also referred to as reliability

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper focuses on predicting bus travel time to improve the reliability of bus services, which falls directly under the Transportation sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote:
This work empirically compares
probabilistic models for the prediction of the conditional probability density function (PDF) of
the travel time and proposes a simulation framework taking as input the latter distributions
to approximate the expected secondary delays, a measure of the reliability of public transport
services

applications.justification: The optimization of bus routes and schedules can be a step towards autonomous buses.
applications.quote:
This work aims at providing tools to measure, and eventually improve, the
reliability of one of the outputs of the service planning phase, namely vehicle schedules
